venue.name: Ahtsik Native Art Gallery
venue.description: Ahtsik Native Art Gallery is a First Nations owned gallery on Pacific Rim Highway in Port Alberni, founded in 2008 by Nuu-chah-nulth master carver Gordon Dick. It represents First Nations artists practicing traditional Northwest Coast art from across British Columbia, with work from Nuu-chah-nulth, Kwakiutl and Coast Salish nations. Gordon Dick runs his studio and carving shelter on the same site and encourages visitors to stop in and watch him work. The gallery is open by appointment or chance, and the site does not describe any program, rate or booking route for school or daycare groups.
venue.address: 7133A Pacific Rim Highway, Port Alberni, British Columbia, Canada V9Y 8Y4

programs.name: Gallery and studio visit
programs.description: The gallery is open by appointment or chance at 7133A Pacific Rim Highway, off Highway 4 on Tseshaht traditional territory. Gordon Dick operates his studio and carving shelter on the same site and encourages visitors to stop in and watch him work. The site publishes no admission price, no group rate, no minimum age, no capacity and no separate booking route for children's groups.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the gallery looking at Northwest Coast carvings by Nuu-chah-nulth, Kwakiutl and Coast Salish artists, in red cedar, alder, cedar bark and bronze. Then stop in at the carving shelter and studio, where Gordon Dick works and talks with visitors about Tseshaht First Nation and about how the carving styles of each region differ.
programs.our_note: The gallery opens by appointment or chance, so phone before you put a group on the bus rather than turning up. Nothing about group size, cost or how long a visit runs is published, so settle all of it on the same call.
programs.practical_summary: The address, phone number and email are published, and the gallery opens by appointment or chance rather than on set hours. Washrooms, parking, indoor lunch space, accessibility and any cost for a group are not stated anywhere on the site, so ask when you phone.
programs.evidence: Gordon Dick operates his studio and carving shelter at Ahtsik Native Art Gallery and encourages visitors to stop in.

gaps: no admission price is published anywhere on the site, for adults, children or groups
no group or school rate is published, and the site never mentions school, daycare or children's groups at all
no youngest age or minimum age for visitors is stated
no capacity limit for a group is stated
no lead time is stated; the only hours information is "By appointment or chance", so how far ahead a group must arrange a visit is unknown
no length or duration for a visit is stated
the site lists a phone number and an email address but never says which one to use to arrange a visit, so how you book is left unknown
washrooms are not mentioned anywhere on the site
no indoor lunch space is described
no rain backup is described; the carving shelter is named but the site does not say whether it is enclosed
parking is not mentioned anywhere on the site, and there is nothing about bus or coach access
wheelchair and stroller access are not mentioned anywhere on the site
the site publishes no coordinates, no map embed and no structured address data, so the street address is recorded and lat/lng are left for a geocoding pass
